fields.scenarioTitle: Clearance Time — Evacuation Decision & Vertical Critical-Care Moves
fields.narration: EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 08:00 CDT on Wednesday, September 16, 2026. The night has passed and your midnight decision stands. All ground transfers have stopped. Coastal AirCare 2 flew its last possible mission at 03:40 and is now grounded. Contraflow on US 181 has ended, and TxDOT reports water over the I-37 low points near the Nueces River. Nothing is leaving Corpus Christi by road. Outside, heavy rain bands are crossing the city with gusts to 48 miles per hour, and water is ponding on Ocean Drive in front of the ED entrance. Here is the latest product: 'EXERCISE — HURRICANE QUINLAN INTERMEDIATE ADVISORY NUMBER 18A — NWS NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER MIAMI FL AL172026 — 700 AM CDT WED SEP 16 2026 — MAX SUSTAINED WINDS 120 MPH, MOVEMENT NW 14 MPH. TROPICAL-STORM-FORCE WINDS STILL EXPECTED AT CORPUS CHRISTI AROUND 12:00 CDT. STORM SURGE WARNING: 4 TO 6 FT IN CORPUS CHRISTI BAY. $$ EXERCISE.' H is 12:00 today, four hours from now. The Hurricane Plan's H minus 6 point for Vertical Evacuation Phase 1 was 06:00, two hours ago. Any infant still in the NICU is on floor 2, and any ICU patient still in the unit is on floor 3, where staffing is 1 nurse to 3 patients. Only 2 of the 6 elevators run on generator power. Last April's drill moved 8 ICU patients in 74 minutes, about 9 minutes per patient. 7 West and 6 West both report they are ready to receive. EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE.
worldState: Time is 08:00 CDT, Wednesday, September 16, 2026. H (34-knot winds at Corpus Christi) is forecast for 12:00 CDT today, 4 hours from now.
NHC Intermediate Advisory 18A (07:00 CDT): Quinlan holds 120 mph max sustained winds, moving NW at 14 mph. The Storm Surge Warning stays at 4 to 6 ft for Corpus Christi Bay.

No more transfers out: Coastal AirCare 2 has been grounded since its 03:40 mission, Gulf Coast Critical Transport ground units have stopped, US 181 contraflow has ended, and the I-37 low points near the Nueces River are under water.
Weather at the hospital: heavy rain bands, gusts to 48 mph, water ponding on Ocean Drive at the ED entrance.

The 06:00 H minus 6 deadline for Vertical Evacuation Phase 1 has passed. Unless every patient has already left, the NICU (up to 12 infants, 3 on ventilators) is still on floor 2 and the ICU (up to 19 patients, 6 on ventilators, staffed 1:3) is still on floor 3.
Receiving areas: 7 West (16 bassinets, transport incubators, 4 ventilators, wall gas) for the NICU and 6 West (24 beds, portable telemetry) for the ICU. Both report ready.
Only 2 of 6 elevators run on generator power. Last April's drill pace was 8 ICU patients in 74 minutes, about 9 minutes per patient. The plan targets 90 minutes for the NICU and 3 hours for the ICU.
Bed 3-07 (3 pressors) and Bed 3-14 (proned) are still the highest-risk ICU moves. Beds 3-11 and 3-18 are on contact precautions with different organisms.
fields.facilitatorNote: Before you read the card, apply the 00:00 decision. If players ordered horizontal evacuation, take every patient who left overnight off the NICU and ICU numbers, and tell the room which Gulf Coast Critical Transport ground units and which Coastal AirCare 2 missions ran (no more than 5 ground runs and 2 air missions, with receiving beds capped at the 07:10 RAC board). If they sheltered in place, the census stays at 12 NICU and 19 ICU. Either way, no further transfers are possible. If players ask: at drill pace, 19 ICU patients on 2 elevators take roughly 2 h 50 min of elevator time, which is just inside the 3-hour target only if the elevators are dedicated to these moves and every order and acceptance is ready.

instructorNote: This card forces the vertical move after the H minus 6 point has passed. Watch for the IC to order Vertical Evacuation Phase 1 at once, announce it on radio channel 2 and log the time. The charge nurses should set the move order from the Evacuation Priority List and check whether the 90-minute and 3-hour targets can be met at drill pace. No patient should leave before there is a provider order and a receiving nurse has accepted them by name and bed, and the House Supervisor should take the 2 generator elevators and start the master board.
